events.title: iPhone XR released
events.summary: Apple released the iPhone XR on October 26, 2018 — a lower-cost LCD model with Face ID and the A12 chip.
events.about: The XR brought notch-era design to a mass price point with a single camera and LCD display. Developers treated it as the volume iPhone for testing Face ID layouts without assuming OLED or telephoto hardware.

narrative.whyChosen: The XR spread Face ID and notch layouts to Apple's best-selling price tier.
narrative.whyImportant: A single affordable Face ID phone simplified the mainstream iOS test matrix.
narrative.problemSolved: Notch-era iOS design was limited to expensive OLED models.

events.title: Google Pixel 3 released
events.summary: Google began selling the Google [Pixel] 3 — Night Sight and dual front cameras on Google's flagship.
events.about: [Nexus] and [Pixel] phones were Google's pure-[Android] reference hardware for developers. Night sight and dual front cameras on google's flagship. [AOSP] builds and CTS testing often used [Pixel] devices as the baseline.

narrative.whyChosen: The Google [Pixel] 3 was a flagship Google [Android] reference device.
narrative.whyImportant: [Pixel]/[Nexus] hardware defines the reference [Android] experience for developers.
narrative.problemSolved: [Android] needed first-party reference phones without [OEM] skin fragmentation.
